abstract: UPS announced 12,000 job cuts (2.4% of its 500,000+ global workforce) in January 2024, citing softer demand and higher union labor costs as drivers of a $1 billion cost-reduction initiative. The cuts primarily affect management and salaried positions while excluding union-represented roles, with 75% of reductions planned for the first half of 2024.
keyFindings: UPS cut 12,000 jobs representing 2.4% of its global workforce of over 500,000 employees.
The company cited softer demand and higher union labor costs as reasons for the $1 billion cost-reduction effort in the fourth quarter of 2023.
Job cuts do not affect union-represented roles and are distributed across all functions and geographies.
UPS's fourth-quarter 2023 revenues were $24.92 billion, below the $25.43 billion Wall Street analysts expected.
In July 2023, UPS agreed to a Teamsters contract raising top full-time driver pay to $49 per hour and part-time starting pay to $21 per hour.
methodology: News report based on company earnings call announcement and official company statements; not a research study.
